meta.description: Comprehensive molecular biology toolkit. Use for sequence manipulation, file parsing (FASTA/GenBank/PDB), phylogenetics, and programmatic NCBI/PubMed access (Bio.Entrez). Best for batch processing, custom bioinformatics pipelines, BLAST automation. For quick lookups use gget; for multi-service integration use bioservices.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated data. All examples use valid accession numbers and standard bioinformatics operations.

practice_boundaries.detail: Library wrapper skill, no medical claims or treatment recommendations.

methodological_ground.detail: All bioinformatics patterns follow established best practices. No methodological fallacies detected.

code_usability.detail: All code examples are syntactically correct and executable with proper imports.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of all promised use cases. Examples are accurate and appropriate for complexity.

reliability.note: Troubleshooting section covers common errors. Error handling patterns shown but not comprehensive. Recovery guidance could be more explicit.

performance_context.note: Good progressive disclosure with 7 reference files. SKILL.md at 447 lines is reasonable. Iterator patterns for large files documented.

agent_usability.note: Clear structure with module-based organization. Consistent terminology. Quick examples provided. Feedback design could be more explicit.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language aligned with bioinformatics tasks. Multiple approaches documented for common workflows.

security.note: Credentials properly externalized to Entrez.email. No dangerous patterns. Input validation delegated to library but not explicitly documented.

maintainability.note: Clean modular separation across 7 reference files. Changes well-isolated. No formal test cases provided.

agent_specific.note: Good trigger precision and progressive disclosure. Strong composability. Escape hatches present but could be more explicit. Minor verbosity in SKILL.md.

key_strengths: Comprehensive coverage of Biopython modules with 7 organized reference files
Clear scope boundaries distinguishing from gget and bioservices for appropriate use cases
Excellent modular organization mapping to Biopython's sub-package structure
Strong practical examples demonstrating common bioinformatics workflows
Good security practices with credential externalization documented

recommendations.title: Add explicit error handling patterns
recommendations.problem: Error handling shown in general guidelines but not consistently demonstrated in examples throughout reference files.
recommendations.root_cause: Focus on happy-path workflows without comprehensive failure mode coverage.
recommendations.fix: Add error handling sections to each reference file showing try-except patterns for common failures like network errors, file format mismatches, and missing fields.

recommendations.title: Enhance escape hatch documentation
recommendations.problem: While the skill distinguishes itself from gget and bioservices, explicit 'When NOT to use' guidance is limited.
recommendations.root_cause: Scope definition focused on positive use cases without explicit out-of-scope scenarios.
recommendations.fix: Add a 'When NOT to Use This Skill' section covering: quick single lookups (use gget), multi-database integration (use bioservices), large-scale production pipelines (consider dedicated workflow managers).

recommendations.title: Add formal test examples
recommendations.problem: No example datasets or test cases provided for users to validate their setup.
recommendations.fix: Add tests/ or examples/ directory with: small example FASTA/GenBank files, expected output for canonical operations, Jupyter notebook demonstrating end-to-end workflows.
